findings.detail: A DROP THAT IS CORRECT, REPORTED SO NOBODY 'FIXES' IT. THAT WOULD CREATE A FALSE CREDIT. The line is 'LEVERS READ: none directly -- everything comes off SigState (st.mode, st.d, st.width_units, st.encoder), which build() froze from mode, d and bigram_dim once': the declaration is `none directly`, and `d` appears only in prose describing what src/sig/api.py::build froze earlier. So harvesting `d` here would credit SIG_D to a function that does not read it, which is the ISSUES P1-M80/L20 'NOTHING READ THESE' shape pointed at the contract line instead of at an operator. The only thing genuinely lost on this line is the `none` sentinel, which costs nothing (no package declares a lever named `none`). The correct repair here is the sentinel one -- 'none directly (everything comes off SigState ...)' -- and NOT anything that lifts `d` out of the prose. TOK's `mint_pmin` drop is the same kind of correct-drop for the same reason and I have already preserved it in my own fix.

findings.detail: THE CLASS ITSELF, STATED ONCE SO THE SUPERVISOR CAN DECIDE WHETHER TO ACT ON IT RATHER THAN ON ITS INSTANCES. I did not edit tests/ (hard constraint) and I am not asking for it to be edited blind -- this is a recommendation with its cost attached. The harvester's identifier filter is RIGHT and its own docstring explains why: the whitespace version harvested 111 English words as levers, and packages declare levers named `state`, `read`, `floor`, `path`, `only`, `on`. The gap is that a rejected item is rejected SILENTLY. A one-line addition to tests/test_contract.py::stub_reads -- when a dropped item's FIRST TOKEN is a bare identifier that the package DECLARES as a lever or that a coupling declares as a wire, report it as a finding rather than discarding it -- would have caught all three real instances (TOK dropout, LM ctx, LM mask_dead_rows) and would have produced exactly two false alarms on today's tree, both of which I have identified above (SIG.encode's `d` and TOK's `mint_pmin`, each inside an explicitly NEGATIVE declaration). That is a 3:2 signal ratio on a check whose whole purpose is to make silent drops loud, and both false alarms are one-line suppressions ('none directly' and 'are NOT read here' are both greppable forms). I am NOT claiming this is free: it adds a check that can fail on prose, and the K-suite's standing preference is for oracles that cannot be argued with. The alternative, which needs no test edit at all, is to fix the five remaining spellings listed under unfinished and accept that the next one written will be silent again.
